target_customer: Diagnostic laboratories, clinics, hospitals, dialysis and veterinary centers in the Philippines and Southeast Asia
problem: Labs and clinics run on manual or fragmented processes for check-in, results, reporting and billing; Dashlabs offers cloud lab and clinic management software integrated with instruments.
business_model: B2B SaaS subscription for laboratory information and clinic management
product_category: Laboratory information system and clinic management software

founders.name: Bryan Giger
founders.background_notes: YC page lists name and title only.

competitors.name: CrelioHealth
competitors.what: Laboratory information system vendor based in Quezon City, Philippines

competitors.name: HiAdvance
competitors.what: Manila based healthcare software company with LIS

technical_complexity.rationale: Integrations with lab analyzers and DICOM imaging devices plus billing and result workflows; standard engineering with hardware integration complexity.

defensibility.rationale: Instrument integrations and lab data create lock-in once deployed; reported COVID testing scale helped early customer references.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: The Department of Health is rolling out its own integrated lab information system, a possible substitute; no dated source of incumbents copying Dashlabs.

market_need_then: The COVID-19 pandemic drove huge testing volume in the Philippines; a company case study says Dashlabs supported the Philippine Red Cross to reach 1.2 million tests in under five months (company claim, January 2021).

branding.domain_note: Uses dashlabs.ai; BuiltWith shows redirects from dashboardlabs.io (first seen 2020), dashboard.holdings and lab.management.

identity.voice_and_tone: Practical and healthcare focused, slogan Digitize, Automate, Simplify Healthcare

branding.community_and_virality: Company blog with COVID testing case studies; no merch or community found.

brand_strength.rationale: Little press on the brand itself; name resembles other Dash Labs companies and is generic.

outcome_analysis: Dashlabs built lab software during the COVID testing surge, raised a reported PHP 65 million seed in early 2022 and now claims 350+ organizations and 20 million patients processed across several Southeast Asian markets. It remains active with about 30 staff. No exit or shutdown found.
notes: Funding: Esquire Philippines (February 15, 2022) and Manila Bulletin reported a PHP 65 million seed (roughly 1.3 million USD); I did not open either article, only search summaries and the YC page headlines. Seedtable lists about 1.3M USD in November 2021 and CB Insights 130K in February 2021 (aggregators). Amount in USD left null because the stated figure is in pesos and I do not convert. The round source_url is the Seedtable page that cites the Manila Bulletin report; treat as weakly sourced. Competitor sources are undated vendor listings in a market report, dated by founding year only.
